attacks.claim: The embargo badge text is hardcoded white on a background that resolves to white in the default light theme, so the label is effectively invisible and fails WCAG 1.4.3. The hardcoded color also bypasses the theme tokens.

The unpublish control is a span with only an onClick handler. It is not focusable and does not respond to Enter or Space, so keyboard-only editors cannot reach the one-click unpublish action (WCAG 2.1.1).

The unpublish control is icon-only with no accessible name. The icon is aria-hidden and the span has no role, aria-label, or visually hidden text, so assistive tech announces nothing meaningful (WCAG 4.1.2, 1.1.1).
attacks.evidence: <TrashIcon aria-hidden="true" /> inside the span, with no aria-label or sr-only text

attacks.claim: handleUnpublish awaits onUnpublish with no try/catch and no error state. A failed request becomes an unhandled rejection, and the editor gets no feedback that the story is still live.

Unpublishing removes the story only from the site. The PR does not address copies already sent downstream (syndication feeds, partner distribution, push notifications, CDN caches), so an early-released story can remain visible after the action.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: no handling of syndication, feeds, notifications, or cache invalidation. Confirm body only says: will be removed from the site and returned to drafts.

attacks.claim: The unpublish control has no pending or disabled state while the request is in flight, so repeated activation could send duplicate unpublish calls. The diff gives no idempotency guarantee.
After confirmation the artifact shows no row update (status or badge change) once onUnpublish resolves, so editors may not know the unpublish took effect.
Unpublish attempts, successes, and failures are not logged or audited in this change, which leaves no trail for a destructive, publicly visible action.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: any logging, metric, or audit event in handleUnpublish or the API it calls

attacks.claim: The embargo state is computed from the client clock on each render and never refreshed, so a badge can remain after the lift time passes, and a skewed client clock can show the wrong status.
attacks.evidence: const embargoed = draft.embargoUntil !== null && new Date(draft.embargoUntil) > new Date();

attacks.claim: The destructive unpublish control ships on every published row with no feature flag or kill switch, so rolling back a misbehaving action requires a redeploy.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: any feature flag or configuration gating the unpublish control

attacks.claim: The control has only a hover style and no :focus-visible rule, so keyboard focus would be invisible even if the control became focusable.
attacks.evidence: .unpublish:hover { color: var(--danger); background: var(--surface-hover); } with no focus rule

attacks.claim: A trash icon reads as delete, not return-to-drafts, which makes a reversible action look riskier and may discourage its use. A label or unpublish-specific icon would match the action.
attacks.evidence: <TrashIcon aria-hidden="true" /> with confirm body: returned to drafts

attacks.claim: The embargo time has no timezone label and no year, so readers outside the newsroom timezone, or reading a lift date in a later year, may misread it.
The amber pair (#b45309 light, #f59e0b dark) is asserted as the outline design with no contrast measurement against the surfaces, so non-text contrast of the outline is unverified.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: contrast measurements for --warn against --surface in either theme

attacks.claim: The claim that the badge shows the lift time in the newsroom timezone depends on formatInNewsroomTz, whose implementation and tests are not in the diff.
attacks.evidence: import { formatInNewsroomTz } from "../lib/time"; (no lib/time change or test shown)

attacks.claim: Each row calls useConfirm() and creates new Date() objects on every render with no memoization or virtualization, which adds overhead for large queues.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: React.memo or list virtualization; const confirm = useConfirm(); new Date(...) > new Date() per row

attacks.claim: Embargo logic (the check and the formatting, with a non-null assertion) is inline in the component and cannot be tested without mocking global time. It should be a pure helper that other queue views can reuse.
attacks.evidence: const embargoed = draft.embargoUntil !== null && new Date(draft.embargoUntil) > new Date(); ... draft.embargoUntil!

attacks.claim: DraftRow gains a required onUnpublish prop, but the diff shows no parent queue change supplying it, so the call-site change is not visible in this PR.
attacks.evidence: onUnpublish: (id: string) => Promise<void>; (no parent change in diff)
